content.title: Warriors Eliminated From Postseason in Play-In Tournament Loss to Suns
content.text: Stephen Curry scored 35 points in 36 minutes, leading the Warriors to a thrilling 126-121 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers at Intuit Dome on Wednesday. Curry exploded for 27 points in the second half, including a 16-point third quarter. His step-back 3-pointer with 50.4 second remaining, his seventh of the game, gave the Warriors a three-point lead that they never relinquished. Al Horford went a perfect 4-for-4 from three in the fourth quarter, hitting big shot after big shot down the stretch. Draymond Green put forth a dominant defensive showing, helping hold All-Star Kawhi Leonard scoreless for 11 minutes of the fourth quarter before his final bucket with 16.9 seconds left and the game already decided. Green had four steals in the game, two of which he took from Leonard in the final minute. "He's a Hall of Fame defender," Kawhi Leonard said of Green postgame. "It was hard to even get shots up."Kristaps Porzingis and Gui Santos both scored 20 points and Brandin Podziemski had 17 points, rounding out a highly-productive outing for a starting lineup that had played just 11 total minutes together coming into the game.Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 0:00Remaining Time 0:00Play-In Tournament Highlights: Golden State Warriors vs. LA Clippers | 4/15/26WEATHERING EARLY CLIPPERS RUNSGui Santos opened the game with a steal and score, but the Clippers would proceed to score the next 12 points, putting the Warriors at an early deficit. The Warriors responded with a 12-2 run to tie the score and a side-step 3-pointer from Stephen Curry — his first field goal of the game — gave them a 17-16 lead. Golden State needed another lengthy run to battle back from an early deficit, as a 13-0 burst propelled them to a 35-31 second-quarter lead. This time, Kristaps Porzingis gave the Warriors the lead with a deep 3-pointer and then he followed it up by dimming up a cutting Gary Payton II for a layup. Their four-point advantage was their largest of the first half — they played from behind for the majority of the time, but these runs helped them remain in striking distance, setting the stage for a late comeback. PORZINGIS SKIES FOR THUNDEROUS DUNKSKristpas Porzingis had a pair of emphatic rim-rocking tip-dunks in the first half. After a missed free throw in the first quarter, Porzingis crashed the offensive glass from beyond the 3-point line, beat everyone to the ball and threw down the poster slam. In the second quarter, Porzingis perfectly timed another offensive rebound off a missed 3-pointer and finished with a powerful two-hand dunk. “He’s a great player, won a championship with Boston and has played in big games,” Kerr said of Porzingis postgame. “Kristaps is a really talented dude — that type of 3-point range, shot blocking, length and IQ. He’s got a great feel and came up big.” Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 0:22Remaining Time 0:22Kristaps Porziņģis hammers it homeCURRY CATCHES FIRE IN THIRD QUARTERStephen Curry scored 16 points in the third quarter, accounting for 16 of the Warriors’ 18 points over a nearly five-minute span. Curry had just two made field goals in nine attempts in the first half and even exited to the locker room after his first quarter stint. For a cold as he was in the first half, he was equally hot in the third quarter, shooting 6-for-8 from the field and 3-for-4 from behind the arc. Curry started with a reverse layup, added a floater and then came off a Draymond Green screen for a four-point play, going on a personal 8-0 run. He would add a step-back mid-range jumper and two 3-pointers to cap a microwave stretch. “It was a beautiful display of competitive will,” Head Coach Steve Kerr said of Curry’s performance. “This is why Steph came back. This is what he does, who he is — if he can compete, he’s going to compete.” Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 1:55Remaining Time 1:55Highlights: Stephen Curry Goes Off for 35 Points in Play-In Tournament Win vs. LA ClippersHORFORD’S PERFECT FOURTH QUARTERThe Warriors trailed by as many as 13 points in the game and had a seven-point fourth-quarter deficit before Al Horford’s first 3-pointer. Playing the two-man game with Stephen Curry, Horford popped out to the perimeter for his first triple with 5:37 remaining. On the ensuing Warriors possession, Gui Santos drove and kicked to Horford for a corner three that pulled the Dubs within three. Horford ended his third straight possession with a 3-pointer — this time Santos found him in the opposite corner. Finally, with the Warriors within a point, Horford splashed in a go-ahead three, assisted by Curry, who thoroughly enjoyed witnessing his splash takeover. “Al Horford — that man has been hurt, in and out of the lineup all year, but when it’s winning time, that’s what champions do,” Curry said postgame. “Nothing but confidence in him. He’s been doing it his whole career, no hesitation. It was beautiful to watch, it was amazing to see the energy in the building when he was hitting those shots.” Postgame Warriors TalksUP NEXT The Warriors will head to Phoenix to face Devin Booker and the Suns for a win-or-go-home matchup on Friday. The winner will earn the eighth seed and a spot in the Western Conference playoffs while the loser will be eliminated from postseason contention. The Dubs eliminated the Clippers with Wednesday's win. MORE NOTABLES:With Wednesday’s victory, the Warriors advanced to Friday’s game at Phoenix for the No. 8 seed in the Western Conference Playoffs… This was the Warriors’ first-ever road win in the Play-In Tournament (now 1-2 on the road all-time)… Golden State is 2-3 all-time in Play-In Tournament games.Wednesday marked the Warriors first-ever win at Intuit Dome… During the regular season, the Warriors had not won a road game against the Clippers since 11/28/21, 105-90, losing the last nine meetings away from the Bay Area… Including the regular season, this marked the Warriors’ 38th clutch game and third against the Clippers this season… The Warriors were 17-20 in clutch games during the 2025-26 regular season. The Warriors trailed by as many as 13 points against the Clippers… During the regular season, the Warriors overcame double-digit deficits 13 times (five on the road).Golden State shot 56.6 percent from the field tonight… During the regular season, the Warriors’ season-high field goal percentage was 55.4 percent on 12/31/25 at CHA.The Warriors turned the ball over 20 times tonight… Golden State had a 6-9 overall and 3-8 road record during the 2025-26 regular season when recording 20-or-more turnovers.Stephen Curry scored a game-high 35 points, his fourth-career 30-point game in the Play-In Tournament… It marked the third-most points he has scored in a Play-In tournament game, behind 39 (2021 vs. Memphis) and 37 (twice, 2021 at Lakers and 2025 vs. Memphis). Gui Santos had 20 points… During the regular season Santos has logged five-career 20-point games (all in 2025-26).Kristaps Porzingis tallied 20 points, five rebounds, five assists… In the regular season Porzingis had one 20/5/5 game, on 3/23/26 at Dallas when he had 22 points, seven rebounds and five assists (21-such games in his career).Al Horford contributed 14 points off the bench, making four 3-pointers… Horford made four-or-more 3-pointers four times during the 2025-26 regular season (Warriors were 3-1 in those games).Draymond Green tallied four steals, his highest total during the 2025-26 regular season was three (four times).
